title: Understanding NumPy Arrays
keywords: numpy arrays and the ndarray model
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of understanding numpy arrays and name one situation where it is useful.
Apply what an array represents to a small NumPy example and inspect the resulting values, shape, or dtype.
Identify one important limitation, boundary case, or validation check for understanding numpy arrays.

content.intro: This lesson develops topic 15 of the supplied curriculum: **Understanding NumPy Arrays**. The main starting point is **What an array represents**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Shape describes how values are arranged; dtype describes how values are represented. Inspecting both before an operation catches many mistakes early.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Understanding NumPy Arrays** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **What an array represents** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np

a = np.array([1, 2, 3])
b = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
print(a.ndim, b.ndim)

common_mistakes.why: Size counts elements; shape describes axis lengths.
Slicing and transposing can produce non-contiguous views.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect `flags` and `strides` when memory layout matters.
